newsitem.title: USA: Seagull Energy increased reserves in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Seagull Energy increased reserves in 1996.

text.p: Seagull Energy Corp said it ended 1996 with proved reserves of 1.14 trillion cubic feet of natural gas and 68 million barrels of crude oil, condensate and natural gas liquids, or the energy equivalent of 1.55 trillion cubic feet equivalent, an increase of nearly 100 billion cubic feet equivalent over the year-end 1995 total.

At that time, the company said, its proved reserves totaled 1.15 trillion cubic of natural gas and 51 million barrels of oil, condensate and other liquids, or the equivalent of 1.46 trillion cubic feet equivalent.
Seagull said its 1996 proved reserve additions replaced the year's production by more than 160 percent.
It said additions totaled the energy equivalent of 277 billion cubic feet of natural gas, compared with production during the year of 173 billion cubic feet equivalent.

The company said the additions consisted of 137 billion cubic feet equivalent from discoveries, extensions and revisions and 141 billion cubic feet equivalent from property purchases. The company also had dispositions totaling 13 billion cubic feet equivalent during the year.

"In most areas our discoveries added more reserves to the probable category than the immediate contribution to the proved totals," the company said, adding "That gives us confidence that future proved additions will be substantial."
